paragraphs.text: The bow catalogue opens it. Bow to the three-worlds’ Lord, ash-pale, three-eyed, trident-wielding, snake-threaded, moon-crested: I bow. I praise, self-forgetting, white-robed in bite-torn cloth, dancing to the tune of the skull-garland: feast-ready. Bow to those whose god is Hara, whose stirs are Hara-fit, Hara-alone-bent breaths ever: fortune’s houses. Your play, behind lordship — and this too, as wished-fulfilled in gifts, by self I reach the supreme means. In Your world-venerated abode, in this play: how great would my bliss-birth be?

The paradox middle. How could He not be fortunate — who is Gauri’s lover, Hara? And how could Hara not be Gauri’s supreme beloved? Whose meditation-nectar is undying, self-rooted, ever-fresh: consciousness-creepers, like some being-tree. At devotion-itch’s showing, Lord’s pillar-firmness arises: by it the world, great festival, is won. Ever to creation-sport, ever seated in staying-pleasure, ever world-eating-sated: to the Master, bow. Nowhere gone, nothing left: who just this, see Your abode as to-be here — fortunate: to them bow, bow. For the devotion-fortuned, what else is begged; for the devotion-poor, what else is begged? Where pains turn pleasures, poison turns nectar, saṃsāra turns liberation: that path is He, Kind-Maker. At root, middle, end: no suffering for Your people — yet we sink, Lord: tell why?

The closing seal. Light is worth begging even by beginners in knowledge-yoga: You, Lord of devotees, are like the light of the free. Devotees have no prayers, no remembrance of You the self — yet this Shiva of theirs, something, on the lip. Who lights all appearances, wrapped in vimarsha: I am this — so I praise Your action-power, Lord. All beings, from BrahmA to Vishnu, being devoured: so I bow, God, to the world as Your-formed. All beyond me is false, by relation to destruction: thus engaged, Lord, by Your destruction-play alone. Meditated, Your form stands present for devotion-rich: unconquered by unthinkable-wonder-makers. By Your devotion-wine-taste nerves’ thrill, night-heroes dance, roused by vetAlas. The praise begun with this limb of mine: by it may all this time be firmly unending.
